source: Pirates. We've been set upon by pirates. Not more than a few hours after we left Danish waters, at that. Their captain calls herself Grace O'Malley, and though she may be coarse, she doesn't seem cruel. Perhaps she can be reasoned with.

source: Hamlet pulled me aside to tell me he's got a plan: when opportunity presents itself, he's going to try and overthrow Grace, leaving Rosie and Guilda to die. This is... worrying. I know there's a bloodless option here—or perhaps something bloodier, depending on how I push my luck. I'm dreading the confrontation.

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: I overheard some of Grace's men discussing her. Such interesting rumors. There's got to be more to find, certainly, and eavesdropping is my specialty. Besides, we're in the middle of the ocean. What else am I to do?

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: I accosted Grace in the captain's quarters about all the rumors I'd heard. To my surprise, she just laughed and suggested she teach me how to hold a blade. She's offered to meet me abovedeck and show me a thing or two. This woman is a whirlwind.

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: As usual, Hamlet ruins everything. That's all I have to update for now. Must go find Grace in her room and apologize. How embarrassing.

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: Grace and I spent the evening drinking and talking. She's nothing like I thought she was. And... at the end of it... we went to bed. We spent the whole night together. I've never experienced anything like this before. I only wish we had more time together. My heart aches for her.

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: Grace and I spent the evening drinking and talking. She's nothing like I thought she was. And... at the end of it... she asked if I wanted to go to bed, though I declined. Nevertheless, it's clear we're kindred souls. I only wish we had more time together.

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: We departed the ship just a few moments ago and were returned to shore via longboat. What a strange journey. I sense there are so many ways that situation could have turned out; I must now reap the consequences of my actions, or else return to the point when Hamlet and I left the docks and try once more.

source: I've agreed to join Grace's crew. I wonder what it would be like, if this was my final fate? To become part of her world of debauchery and action and see where that path might lead...

source: I doubt they would be hanging out among the graves at this hour.
Here is where Bernardo reviews all his paperwork.
And, from the look of it, keeps anything he's confiscated from the other men.
'Philip Martin: he never could pay his bill.'
I'd no idea we buried debtors in the castle yard.
'Marcus Faber: One foot in the heavens, he followed the stars.'
Elegant and inspiring. Lord Faber must have been a dreamer.
'Max Grossman: Here lies a fellow of infinite jest, of most excellent fancy.'
Alas, poor man. I knew him well.
Someone has carved a heart around the names on this one.
'Kim and Dan McAuliffe: In death as in life, adventuring together.'
It's nice to see not all love is fickle.
'Christopher L. Morrow: Urge no more words; I have no more to say.'
There's poetry in that.
'Grace Kelley: Well, that could have gone better.'
I've asked around a bit, trying to figure out what 'that' was. But no one knows, or will tell me.
'Bryant Woods: No great loss...'
Sir Woods must have been serenely humble, then. Or dreadfully boring.
'Joanne Dragich: She thought she could find the cliff in the fog. Unfortunately, she mist.'
And that's why walls were built around the castle's cliff edge.
'Sarah Villegas: HOLD MY MEAD.'
Those were her last words. Some are ruminating on their meaning still.
'Kris Evans: Evs got sick and tired of rating: Died from an overdose of grading.'
Hmm. I've never heard of that device in the dungeons before.
'Jesse Schell: PERICVLA VERITATI SAEPE CONTIGVA.'
'The truth is often dangerous.' Would that everyone had learned this lesson.
'Sunny Hazzard: R.I.P. Sunny, too sweet for this world.'
The sweet are often the flowers that sooner drop their petals.
Yorick's grave. He was the jester when I was young.
He was buried in the royal graveyard at King Hamlet's request. The family was quite fond of him.
These are the royal family graves. The one in the center is Hamlet's father, King Hamlet.
Gertrude will soon be buried alongside him.
Some day, Hamlet, the Queen, and the King will all find rest here.
'Lady Simona of Denmark.'
The words on this tombstone have worn away with time...
On occasion, I like to write here. It's been a while since I had the time, though.
This is where I'd seat visitors for a chat... that is, if Father ever allowed me to have any.
It's locked.
That door's locked.
I ought not to leave just yet.
The guards have locked up their chambers for the night.
Leartes locked the door. I guess he wants his privacy.
Hamlet's locked the door. I should... probably leave him be.
The bar is closed. Othello has left by now.
The castle cutlery. Irma keeps it spotless every night.
All of Irma's various pots and pans.
One of the guard's beds.
It's... much less nice than mine.
Hmm. 'A Treatise on Divine-Given Morality.'
I had no idea our guard staff were so well read.
And there's a second book underneath. Oh, it's got illustrations in it.
What is that woman doing?
I take back what I said before.
When some new man joins the unit, they'll put their personal items here.
Playing cards, and winnings.
I'm surprised Marcellus just leaves this all out in the open.
Horatio's personal effects are here, what little of them he has.
He's not strictly a guard, but the King gave him quarters on Hamlet's request.
More convenient than staying at the inn down the hill, I suppose.
There are thousands of books in here. I could spend years looking through them all.
...Of course, some of them are so old they might disintegrate into dust if I touched them.
It's my mother, Elise. I think some travelling artist painted this for my father.
It's strange, but I don't remember her face very well... I only see my reflection in her portrait.
What's this?
This all seems so trivial...
But I can't stop reading.
Hard to believe Father has something like this in his room.
Ah. I borrowed this from the gallery some time ago.
It's certainly not a very uplifting tale.
I wish this story didn't feel so terribly familiar somehow.
It's a book of poetry.
Persephone... A girl taken from her homeland and made a Queen.
Sounds familiar.
This gate leads out of town to the countryside. There's nothing that way but a lot of fields.
Lady Edith, often called 'The Brilliant.'
She was renowned for her great intellect and keenly inquisitive nature—not to mention her morbid sense of humor.
When I struggled with Latin as a girl, my father often jokingly told me to come down here and ask this portrait for advice.
The late King Hamlet's portrait used to be here, but someone—Hamlet, actually—has gone and torn it off the wall. He's so strange.
We're so much alike, you and I.
This noblewoman lived long before me. Her name is rubbed off the plaque, but there's a bit of a poem scrawled onto the corner...
'My beloved hometown, the sweetfish river running through it...'
...Never could make sense of that.
It's a picture of a foreign castle.
'Wiener Neustadt, the site of the court of Maximilian I, for Queen Gertrude of Denmark on her birthday.'
Hmm. I suppose this is where Gertrude was raised.
Lady Gina of Denmark. She was known, I'm told, for her unfailing kindness.
Prince Max, a distant relative of Hamlet. His performance in hunting, jousting, and other sport was considered legendary.
I've always thought his portrait was rather handsome.
King James, I believe. A gentle king who was well respected in his time.
That portrait of Queen Gertrude was painted when she was just a little older than I am now—on the day of her first wedding.
That's King Alexander, Hamlet's grandfather. He's... intimidating. I wonder what happened to him.
Prince Florizel. Word has it that he fell in love with a shepherdess and renounced his claim to the throne to make her his wife.
King Douglas. He was a well-humored man and a scholar, noted for his many contributions to this library—among others.
He was a teacher to many, I'm told.
Hello, little one.
This one looks like it's been eating extra kitchen scraps...
